components.explanation: The three props as Godot imports them: waystone.glb, teleport_circle.glb and spikes.glb (binary glTF exported from Blender with +Y Up by tools/blender/export_glb.py) and their .import settings. Each origin is the centre of its underside; sizes and budgets come from CHANGE-BRIEF.md.

The small 3D scene: project.godot (main scene, Forward Plus, window size), scenes/props_room.tscn (floor, one light, a camera, the three props at Y = 0 and a 1.2 m post for Rudy's height) and tools/build_props_room.gd, the headless script that builds it.

tests/check_props.gd: the headless check. Part 1 measures each .glb on its own (bounding box against the brief within 5 mm, height on Y, origin at the underside centre, node scale and rotation, triangles, colours); part 2 checks each prop's lowest point against the floor mesh's top in the scene.

tests/capture_props.gd: renders the running scene in a window from five views for TEST-REPORT.md. Its first version read the camera before the scene was in the tree, one of the three things Claude got wrong. The film's orbit uses a separate film-only driver on an isolated copy (capture/orbit_driver.gd).

code_result_pairs.observation: The real main scene res://scenes/props_room.tscn in Godot 4.7.2 Forward+, Movie Maker at 3840×2160, 30 fps: 45 frames on the scene's own camera, a 600-frame orbit at its radius (4.6 m) and height (2.2 m), 45 frames back home. All three props stand on the floor with shadows from their bases; the waystone's back is plain.

Recorded headless output on an isolated copy of godot/ at f6f8acf: the three bounding boxes match the brief to four decimals, heights on Y, origins at (0, 0, 0), 118/130, 280/300 and 82/100 triangles; 44 ok lines, PASS: 0 failed check(s), exit code 0.

Recorded output: the scene as built passes (lowest point 0.0000 m); an isolated copy with the waystone's transform Y set to 0.3 reports 'FAIL Waystone sits on the floor (lowest point 0.3000 m above the floor's top)', 'FAIL: 1 failed check(s)', exit code 1.
